meta.note: Server-side use is out of scope and cannot be known from the client. 'purpose' describes what the client-side check can distinguish, not proven server scoring. 'observed' = the field changed in our offline diff runs when the cited dimension changed; 'code' = the client code explicitly compares or derives against the cited reference; 'inferred' = hypothesis from the API used.

purposeBasisLevels.observed: changed in our offline diff runs when the cited dimension changed
purposeBasisLevels.code: client code explicitly compares/derives against the cited reference
purposeBasisLevels.inferred: hypothesis from the API used; not proven

whyByCategory.win: Probe 1 inverts Object.getOwnPropertyNames(window) into buckets. The set of globals is a build/version fingerprint, and automation frameworks, injected scripts and hooks add or remove globals; in our runs individual buckets moved with the webdriver flag, hook injection, headless mode and UA preset. The iframe-realm checks compare a fresh realm with the main one.
whyByCategory.worker: Probes 2, 4, 5, 34 and 36 run code in a Worker and send its navigator/hardware view next to the main-thread one. Spoofing usually patches only the main realm, so a worker reply that disagrees (UA, cores, memory) exposes it; the worker reply moved with UA and hardware changes in our diffs.
whyByCategory.math: Math precision on fixed inputs is constant per engine/CPU and acts as an engine check that should match the claimed UA. bmma1 is an eval/global-this consistency number that probe 27 compares with slot 21 (VM anti-tamper).
whyByCategory.env: The envelope (tag, config blob, status, start/end/duration, executor) is bookkeeping: it tells the server which probes ran, whether they failed and how long they took. Durations double as a weak timing signal; status codes change when a probe throws (e.g. under hooks).
whyByCategory.nav: The UA string and high-entropy client hints are reported side by side so they can be checked against each other and against engine behaviour; client hints moved with the UA preset in our diffs. The keyboard layout map adds per-machine entropy and differed in headless mode.
whyByCategory.dom: The DOM behaviour battery, image-load checks and <html> attribute list distinguish real rendering engines from emulated/headless ones and detect attributes injected by extensions or hooks (observed under hook injection).
whyByCategory.font: Installed fonts and text metrics are classic per-machine entropy; the font-probe timing lists are run-to-run timing data.
whyByCategory.net: Connection type and online state describe the network profile; plausibly compared with the IP's network type server-side (not knowable).
whyByCategory.stack: Error().stack line:column positions move when the challenge script is wrapped or code is injected (observed under hook injection and stack-limit changes). Probe 37 traps console/devtools, Proxy and toString, which change when harness wrappers are visible.
whyByCategory.gfx: WebGL vendor/renderer, parameters and canvas pixels identify the GPU stack; they moved with GPU readback changes, and headless/software-GL modes produce distinctive values.
whyByCategory.loc: Timezone, Intl formatting and historical Date offsets give locale entropy and can be checked against the IP's geography server-side; they moved with timezone and locale changes in our diffs.
whyByCategory.hash: Audio-render digests are device entropy. The four SHA-256 digests of fixed inputs are constants: they only confirm that crypto.subtle behaves like a real browser.
whyByCategory.perf: Navigation timing, body sizes, Trusted Types/nonce checks and navigation type describe how the page was loaded, whether it was rewritten, and whether it is a reload/replay.
whyByCategory.media: WebRTC offer/ICE and codec lists expose network interfaces and the media stack; they help detect proxies/VMs and add entropy.
whyByCategory.page: PUUDF8 page info is supplied by the challenge page and echoed back to bind the payload to it; its page-fingerprint and script-length counters changed when scripts were injected.
whyByCategory.dev: Media queries, battery and permission states are device/display entropy; permission and battery states are commonly abnormal in headless/VM setups (hypothesis).
whyByCategory.native: Probe 27 tests a long list of native functions for patches: .arguments access, prototype===undefined, own property names and toString containing "[native code]". These lists changed under the hook modes in our diff runs.
whyByCategory.ctx: Members of the server's challenge object are echoed back so the payload is bound to this challenge instance; serialized state strings carry the same binding.
whyByCategory.time: Differences between challenge timestamps and Date.now() at send show how old the challenge is (freshness/replay); performance.now() deltas add execution-timing data.
